sources.title: Comune di Baranello: Zona archeologica di Monte Vairano
sources.note: Municipal archaeological description: settlement walls, house beside southern gate, floor, plaster, domestic finds and cistern. Erroneous conversion of building measurements into Oscan feet is not used.

sources.title: University of Padua, TESS: Campobasso floor catalogue
sources.note: Indexed record 3, Baranello, Monte Vairano, casa di LN: coins in floor preparation date the floor to 214 to 150 BCE. Direct page retrieval failed; indexed institutional text was read.

sources.title: Direzione regionale musei nazionali Molise: Santuario italico
sources.note: Indexed official site description: fifth-century visitation, fourth-century buildings, late-second/early-first-century BCE theatre-temple, political functions, sculpted seating and Domus Publica. Direct retrieval timed out; indexed text was read.

sources.title: Katherine McDonald: Four footprints, two languages, one tile, 2016
sources.note: Linguist’s interpretation of Pietrabbondante roof tile c.100 BCE, Oscan/Latin inscriptions and shoeprints. Enslaved or possibly freed women; Detfri may be a name or designation. Short transliteration and translation quoted; no exact original-script reconstruction attempted.

sources.title: Scuola Normale Superiore, Mnamon: Oscan
sources.note: Alessia Ventriglia, English translation Melanie Rockenhaus: regional alphabets and media of Oscan inscriptions, fourth to first centuries BCE.

sources.title: Icaro, Alemán and Viciano: Stable Isotopes Unveil Dietary Trends, 2023
sources.note: Biology 12, 1382. Uses Opi Val Fondillo sixth/fifth-century BCE context and cautious discussion/conclusions about terrestrial foods and variable nitrogen results only. Does not adopt speculative fish identifications or problematic general historical introduction.

sources.title: Fabius Maximus Rullianus and the capture of Gavius Pontius: Livy’s book 11 and the last years of the Third Samnite War
sources.note: Bulletin of the Institute of Classical Studies 68/3. Final discussion: 291 Venusia colony, 290 campaign, treaty and probable subordination within Rome’s alliances; ancient narrative limitations remain explicit.

sources.title: Josiah Osgood: The Spiral of Violence, in Rome and the Making of a World State
sources.note: Sections The Bull Gores the Wolf and later civil-war narrative: Samnite participation, citizenship legislation, continued resistance and alliance with Marius. Political transition is not population disappearance.

proposedOverrides.summary: Samnite communities built hilltop settlements and public sanctuaries. Household finds reveal food and weaving, while a later roof tile preserves workers’ writing and shoeprints. Their history continued well beyond the map’s early window.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Index c.500 to323BCE. Decoded BCE500/BCE400 polygons share bounds13.638736 to16.151562E,40.746513 to42.039127N. Broad central/southern Italian cultural footprint, not a certified unitary state border. Later house floor214 to150BCE, sanctuary late2nd/early1stBCE and writing c.100BCE are explicitly labelled later history. Roman political change is not extinction.
